title: PaperBirch ops — raw integration call notes
body:
Attendees: Asha (SE), Lina (CSM - PaperBirch), Owen (PaperBirch infra lead), Marcus (runtime eng), 2x PB infra engineers

Purpose: capture raw requirements + unexpected operational constraints from PB ops call on 2025-11-07. Note: lots of half-answers — treat as discovery raw notes.

Customer context (brief): PaperBirch is a regional consumer finance platform with strict PII residency, uses private cloud colo + some AWS accounts in eu-west-1, onboarding for two feature sets: 1) intelligent KYC triage (chat + redaction) 2) semantic search over transcripts (embeddings + reranking). They want Private (VPC) deployment with HSM/KMS integration, reserved capacity for peak batch hours, and token-level billing reconciliation with internal cost center tags.

What they said / requirements (as stated in call):
- Must support FIPS 140-2 HSM; prefer HSM-backed key wrap for model prompt seed encryption.
- On-prem package must run on their RHEL 8 clusters (no systemd customizations allowed).
- Data plane traffic must not traverse public internet — VPC peering or PrivateLink only.
- Per-route rate limits: different teams (KYC vs search) require separate quotas and separate cost centers. Need per-route token accounting exported as CSV daily.
- 99.95% uptime target for dedicated night-batch windows (01:00-05:00 local) — they will pay for reserved capacity but expect auto-burst for sudden surges.
- Latency SLO for KYC chat: 300ms p50 for short prompts (<256 tokens), p95 < 800ms.
- Support for embeddings pipeline: want 8-bit quantized model to run on T4-equivalent nodes for cost reasons.
- KV cache persistence: they prefer sticky session affinity for chat threads to avoid cold KV recomputation.

Observed gotchas / constraints from PB infra:
- Network MTU on colo is 9000; they saw packet fragmentation when we trialed our default UDP health checks — need to confirm our probes don't assume 1500 MTU.
- Existing security team blocks new IP ranges without a signed FEDRAMP-style questionnaire. Timeline for approvals is 3–4 weeks.
- Their logging stack (self-hosted ELK) has 30GB/day ingestion cap; cannot ship full token-level logs. They asked for sampled token traces + compact cost reports.
- They run strict SELinux policies. Installer must not rely on permissive modes.

Technical clarifications we need (follow up items):
- KMS/HSM: which vendor? Owen said they use Azure Key Vault HSM and a Thales Luna in their colo — need exact APIs and whether they allow PKCS#11. Action: Marcus to confirm KMS adapter surface we support and drop-in instructions (due 2025-11-21).
- RHEL packaging: they have internal policy avoiding systemd unit modifications. Action: Owen to share internal packaging checklist + install script constraints (link expected).
- Per-route accounting: Lina asked if we can export a CSV with columns: date, route_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, cost_usd, cost_center_tag. Action: Asha to prototype export schema and sample file (due 2025-11-14).
- Quantization profile: they asked if we support GPT-style model quantization to 8-bit and how that affects quality for embeddings. Action: Marcus + Applied ML to run 2 model quality experiments vs float baseline and produce a short eval (due 2025-11-28).

Immediate operational risks flagged in call:
- Billing mismatch risk: PB expects token accounting to match their internal token-metering tool (homegrown). We need to reconcile our tokenization algorithm and include serializer details (e.g., Unicode normalization, prompt concatenation order). Potential for 0.5–1.5% discrepancy on long batch jobs.
- Failover semantics: PB wants deterministic fallback: if primary private cluster saturated, route to Redwood hosted as DR. But their compliance team forbids cross-border data. We must implement per-customer policy toggle to disable hosted DR.
- Cold-start throughput: the embeddings pipeline will run large one-off batches (500k texts). Need advice on split/batching and best-effort resume if interrupted.

Suggested technical approach (high-level):
- Private deployment (VPC) with dedicated pool (reserved), autoscale policy configured with burst ceiling and pre-warm windows aligned to PB batch windows. Offer a two-tier model: quantized variant (cost-efficient) + float fallback (quality).
- Implement per-route meters in the agent sidecar that emits daily CSVs and a summarized JSON (for internal dashboard). Include tokenization metadata header for reconciliation.
- Provide an installer artifact (RPM) that adheres to RHEL 8 packaging constraints and SELinux enforcement. Use systemd units but no override of existing policies; provide documentation for system admins to integrate.
- HSM integration: support PKCS#11 and Azure Key Vault on day-1, include a sample KMS config with example aliases.

Notes for sales / contract team:
- Need to capture a clause around DR routing (explicit opt-in).
- Reserved capacity pricing: propose committed monthly baseline + burst credits. Customer asked for example TCO numbers for 100M tokens/month embedding + 10M tokens/month chat. Marcus to send back ballpark.

Next steps / owners (quick):
- Asha: prototype CSV export schema + short note on tokenization differences (due 2025-11-14).
- Marcus: confirm KMS/HSM plugin surface + start quant eval (due 2025-11-21 for adapter details, 2025-11-28 for quant eval).
- Owen (PB): share internal install checklist and KMS vendor contact (due 2025-11-14).
- Lina: coordinate contract language re: DR opt-in and data residency (due 2025-11-18).
- Ops sync: schedule 30m follow-up with PB infra to walk through installer (tentative 2025-11-18). Asha to propose times.

Loose thoughts / back-of-envelope items to capture:
- If we need to avoid token-level logs, we can provide sampled token traces + compact prompt/response hashes for debugging. Include an option to redact PII before shipping traces.
- For large embedding batches, recommend clients push partitioned jobs (multipart upload + resumable checkpoint index). Could expose simple CLI helper script in our client SDK.
- Consider adding an explicit "no-hosted-fallback" flag per customer in the control plane for legal constraints. Small feature but high value.

Unresolved questions (to raise in next call):
- Does PB require data-at-rest encryption using customer managed keys across all ephemeral artifacts (KV cache snapshots)?
- Are there latency constraints for embeddings indexing step (they expect indexing within 2 hours of ingestion)?
- What is their tolerance for 8-bit quantization quality drop for reranking?

Quick log of Slack threads and tickets raised during call:
- Slack: #pb-onboarding Asha -> "need HSM adapter details" (2025-11-07)
- Jira: PB-3172 created for installer checklist follow-up

End raw notes. Save & move into deeper follow-up doc after Marcus sends quant eval and Asha prototypes CSV.
